hypothesis: Consecutive-loss streak + tight-spread conditioned skip: skip the open leg of an oracle signal when EITHER (a) the last 2 consecutive closed positions both had negative estimated PnL (streak signal), OR (b) current spread > 1.1x rolling 60-tick median (spread signal). Reduce-only orders always execute. The streak captures serial correlation in adverse oracle regimes; the spread filter removes adverse entry moments where oracle reliability is lower.
notes: PASS -- 12-date train window (20260308-20260320, 12 trading days): streak-spread-tight $4772.0/106428 trades vs simple $1984.0/132536 trades; delta_pnl=+140.52%, well above +5.0% gate. Win rate: 37.1% vs 35.6% (+1.5pp). Max drawdown: -1.41% vs -3.77% (improved). Skip rate: 19.7% (26,108 fewer trades). Improvement consistent across ALL 12 dates. Config: sigma=5, seed=42, horizon=30s. Slippage: both 0.0 (zero fill-cost model, see research/NOTES.md).

hypothesis: Stack two gates on OPEN-leg orders: (1) positional gate (position_cap=1) blocks the doubled-up netting-OMS cascade entry; (2) top-of-book imbalance gate skips entries where bid/(bid+ask) is materially adverse to the trade direction (skip_threshold=0.40, min_total_size=2). Reduce-only orders always execute. Builds on position-tier-gate (pnl=4262.50 baseline-of-baseline) by adding a P&L-correlated entry filter; expected to drop losing trades preferentially via the Lipton-Pesavento short-horizon mid-direction signal, lifting realized P&L while reducing trade_count.

hypothesis: Refinement of position-tier-imbalance-gate. Replace the SINGLE-tick top-of-book imbalance read with a short-horizon EMA-smoothed imbalance (alpha=0.30, ~6-tick equivalent window) updated incrementally on each quote tick. All other gates inherited verbatim: positional cap=1 (cascade protection), reduce-only fast-path (intraday_flat), thin-book guard min_total_size=2, threshold=0.40. Motivation: single-tick imbalance is noisy at the quote-by-quote level; Lipton-Pesavento and Kolm/Turiel/Westray both place the natural alpha horizon of book/order-flow signals at multi-tick (~2 price changes). EMA smoothing should give a more reliable read of the persistent book lean and preferentially keep good trades while filtering adverse-lean entries.

hypothesis: Refinement of position-tier-imbalance-ema-gate. Replace the static/EMA-smoothed top-of-book imbalance gate with a rolling-window Order Flow Imbalance (OFI) gate per Cont/Kukanov/Stoikov 2014: per-tick OFI events e_n (signed bid/ask add+cancel deltas) accumulated in a 10s window; BUY orders skip when window-summed OFI <= -2.0 (book bleeding away from bids / building on asks = adverse to buying), SELL orders skip when summed OFI >= +2.0. All other gates inherited verbatim: positional cap=1 (cascade protection), reduce-only fast-path (intraday_flat), thin-book guard min_total_size=2.0. Motivation: static imbalance captures the level of bid/ask size at a single tick (noisy point read); OFI captures order-book flow over a short horizon and is shown empirically to be a substantially stronger short-horizon mid-direction predictor (Cont et al. 2014; Kolm/Turiel/Westray 2021). Iter-2 noted that incremental smoothing of the static signal was exhausted within the position_cap=1 stack and recommended a structural signal-class change; OFI is that change.

The OFI gate is STRUCTURALLY WORSE than the static/EMA imbalance gate within this position_cap=1 stack on this train window; it does NOT meet ANY refinement-axis target in config.yaml->refinement (min_sharpe_delta=+0.5 missed; min_pnl_delta_pct=+2.0 missed; min_winrate_delta_pp=+2.0 missed; min_mdd_delta_pp=-1.0 missed). Plausible causes (declining priority, not verified): (a) the 10s OFI window aliases with the 30s oracle horizon and blocks entries during exactly the flow regimes the oracle is fading; (b) flow_threshold=2.0 was calibrated for aggressor-flow-gate's trade-tape signal, not quote-tick OFI which accumulates faster and reaches |2| in a noisier regime; (c) MES is thin top-of-book so most ticks add 0 or 1 to OFI and the deque is barely smoother than a single-tick view. Verdict robust to the missing 03-19 date: even at the extreme assumption that the algo would add 0 P&L on that day, delta-vs-baseline remains in the +5000% region; vs-iter-2 regression direction would also be unchanged. Trade count HIGH (56k+), not low-trade-count flagged. Config: sigma=6, seed=42, horizon=30s; position_cap=1, flow_threshold=2.0, window_seconds=10.0, min_total_size=2.0.

hypothesis: Structural test of the position-tier gate's binding direction. Relax position_cap from 1 to 2 while inheriting position-tier-imbalance-ema-gate (iter-2 best) verbatim for every other component (EMA imbalance gate, thin-book guard, reduce-only fast-path). Tests whether cap=1 is the actual local optimum or merely a sufficient guard against the doubled-up netting-OMS cascade. If cap=2 also blocks the cascade while admitting profitable additional accumulation on sustained signals, pnl should rise; if cap=1 is the binding optimum, pnl should fall.

hypothesis: Structural axis change vs iter-2 best (position-tier-imbalance-ema-gate). Stack a short-window realized-vol regime gate on top of iter-2's algorithm: per quote tick, compute pstdev of mid log-returns over the last vol_window=60 quote ticks (O(1) via running sum and sum-of-squares), sample that short-vol into a baseline deque every vol_sample_every=10 quote ticks (length baseline_window=300). For OPEN-leg orders, if current short-vol > vol_multiplier=1.5 * baseline_median_vol, SKIP. All other gates inherited verbatim: position_cap=1, EMA-imbalance gate (alpha=0.30, threshold=0.40, min_total_size=2.0), reduce-only fast-path (intraday_flat). The structural change is the gate AXIS: from single-tick book imbalance (microstructure noise) to short-horizon realized vol (regime). Per iter-4's takeaway recommending a structurally different axis.

POSITIVE-INFORMATION RESULT: the vol-regime axis and the EMA-imbalance axis filter approximately the same marginal slice of entries on this train window -- additional symmetric entry gates within the position_cap=1 stack have diminishing returns. The next iteration should try an asymmetric/directional vol gate (skip BUYs only when vol high AND mid falling; skip SELLs only when vol high AND mid rising) OR move to a structurally different mechanism such as time-of-day filter or reduce-only delayed execution. Per OBJECTIVE.md sec.6, PASS-vs-baseline holds even when refinement targets miss; this algo is logged as a PARALLEL passing algorithm but should NOT be treated as an improvement over iter-2.
